title: Signature Object graph parsing — PDF Structure Extractor
description: Signature original — PDFs are graphs of numbered indirect objects linked by references. Parsers build the object map before reading content. Objects are the atoms. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
demo:
# PDF structure: parse a minimal PDF's objects and extract text-showing operations.
pdf = """1 0 obj<</Type/Catalog/Pages 2 0 R>>endobj\n2 0 obj<</Type/Pages/Kids[3 0 R]/Count 1>>endobj\n3 0 obj<</Type/Page/Parent 2 0 R/Contents 4 0 R>>endobj\n4 0 obj<</Length 20>>stream\nBT (Hello) Tj ET\nendstream\nendobj\ntrailer<</Root 1 0 R>>""".replace("\\n", "\n")
import re
objs = re.findall(r"(\d+) \d+ obj(.*?)endobj", pdf, re.S)
print(f"found {len(objs)} objects")
for num, body in objs:
    texts = re.findall(r"\((.*?)\)\s*Tj", body)
    streams = "stream" in body
    print(f"  obj {num}: text_ops={texts} has_stream={streams}")
trailer = re.search(r"/Root\s+(\d+)", pdf)
print("catalog object:", trailer.group(1) if trailer else "not found")
provenance: Signature-authored original method created for the JAH archive toolkit; clearly labeled Signature, not a public record.
